extracted.subtask_description: A news style and usage guide for reporting on diverse peoples, religions, disabilities, cultures and sensitive topics, with recommended terminology, capitalization, context and cautions to ensure accurate, non-stigmatizing coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: reservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Indian reservations are areas of land reserved by the U.S. government as permanent tribal homelands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'reservation' to refer to these areas; note historical policy origin (1787), number (326 in 2015), acreage (~56 million acres) and that more than 60% of American Indians live away from reservations.

rubrics_metrics.name: residential care homes
rubrics_metrics.description: Residential care homes offer personalized services to small groups of adults who live together in a home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These homes provide lodging, meal services and assistance with daily living activities. Other terms include adult family homes, board and care homes, or personal care homes.

rubrics_metrics.name: retarded
rubrics_metrics.description: See mentally retarded, mentally disabled, intellectually disabled, developmentally disabled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry directs to preferred terminology; 'retarded' is an outdated/offensive term—use people-first and current clinical language.

rubrics_metrics.name: reverse discrimination, reverse racism
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrases used in lawsuits and in accusations that affirmative action disadvantages men and non-minorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research shows this scarcely happens; cite studies (e.g., 1995 Brandeis study) and avoid implying widespread occurrence without evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roma, Romany, Romani
rubrics_metrics.description: The Roma, or Romani (also spelled Romany) are a traditionally itinerant ethnic group, who live mostly in Europe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the term 'Gypsies' (negative connotations and many Roma don't identify with it). Note alternate names (Gitanos in Spain), language origins (links to northern India), not to confuse with Irish Travelers; note historical persecution and ongoing discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roman Catholic Church
rubrics_metrics.description: The largest Christian community; considers itself the one, true expression of the church founded by Jesus Christ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain origins (Church of Rome), Petrine/papal authority (Matthew 16:18), historical schism with Orthodox in 11th century, distinction with Protestant 'ecclesial communities', seven sacraments listed, hierarchical structure (pope, cardinal, archbishop, bishop, monsignor, priest, deacon), organizational units (archdioceses, dioceses) and note women are barred from holy orders. Capitalization and context guidance embedded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rosh Hashanah
rubrics_metrics.description: The Jewish New Year, celebrated according to the Hebrew calendar sometime between the middle of September and the middle of October.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pronounced 'rohsh-huh-SHAH-nuh.' For dates, consult Jewish holidays page on Hebcal.

rubrics_metrics.name: rumspringa
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Amish allow their youth, after age 16, to spend a couple years free of the most intense restrictions of their faith while still living with their parents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to ensure commitment before baptism; note that the vast majority decide to remain within the Amish community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Russian Orthodox Church
rubrics_metrics.description: Branch of the Eastern Church of Christianity with headquarters in Moscow; largest of national and ethnic Eastern Orthodox churches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Eastern Orthodox for broader context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sabbath
rubrics_metrics.description: The day of the week observed for rest and worship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most Christian traditions observe on Sunday; Judaism (and some Christian traditions) observe on Saturday. Jews’ observance begins at sundown Friday (often called Shabbat). Capitalize in religious references, lowercase when talking about periods of rest.

rubrics_metrics.name: safe neighborhood, bad neighborhood
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid judgmental terms about neighborhoods or districts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use more specific terms such as low-income neighborhood or areas with high crime rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: safe sex, safer sex
rubrics_metrics.description: Sexual practices that minimize transmission of HIV and other infectious agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some publications prefer 'safer sex' to denote that no sexual contact is completely safe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sambo
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically, term was used to describe a happy black slave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Today it is an offensive term. Do not use in copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: sandsucker
rubrics_metrics.description: Racial slur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sansei, sansei
rubrics_metrics.description: Term for third-generation Japanese Americans, originating from Japanese for 'third generation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain generational terms (Issei, Nisei, Sansei, Yonsei, Gosei), note American context and typical capitalization practices (some institutions capitalize generational terms in generational context; others lowercase when referring to an individual). See Issei/issei, Nisei/nisei, Yonsei/yonsei.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanskrit
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the oldest languages still used; root for many languages and used in religion and ceremony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note characteristics (precise alphabet, compact writing system, complex grammar), scripts (Devanagari used by some Sanskrit-based languages). Link to Omniglot for more.

rubrics_metrics.name: sari (also saree)
rubrics_metrics.description: A traditional garment worn by a woman in India, Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe as about 6 yards of fabric wrapped around the body, usually leaving the midriff bare; note variations in fabric, style, price; sometimes worn with a blouse.

rubrics_metrics.name: schizo, schizoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Slang words derived from schizophrenic and used inaccurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid; instead use accurate words (indecisive, unsettled) when describing nonmedical situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: schizophrenia, schizophrenic
rubrics_metrics.description: A severe and chronic mental illness characterized by distorted recognition and interpretations of reality; does not involve split personalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using 'schizophrenic' as an adjective; refer to a person as diagnosed with schizophrenia or living with schizophrenia. Use people-first language. Do not use for nonpsychiatric conditions. Refer to someone as having schizophrenia only if relevant and formally diagnosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scotch, Scots, Scottish
rubrics_metrics.description: All three can mean 'of or relating to Scotland', but modern usage differs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'Scottish' as adjective for people/culture; 'Scots' often refers to the language/dialect; 'Scotch' generally used for certain food products (Scotch whisky etc.). Be mindful some Scots may take offense at 'Scotch' for people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scottsboro
rubrics_metrics.description: 1931 case where two white women falsely accused nine black teenagers of rape; the case symbolized racism and injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide historical context, multiple retrials, protests, two Supreme Court rulings, partial release after years, and 1976 pardons.

rubrics_metrics.name: sect
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to a group that has broken off from another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid this label unless sure it fits; it often carries negative connotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 8, Housing Choice Voucher Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 8 is shorthand for the Housing Choice Voucher Program funded by HUD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the more accurate and current term 'Housing Choice Voucher Program' when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: secular humanism
rubrics_metrics.description: An outlook that emphasizes human rather than religious values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines values: reason, scientific inquiry, individual freedom and responsibility, human values and compassion, need for tolerance and cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: secularism
rubrics_metrics.description: Belief that religion and religious considerations have no place in public life and education.

rubrics_metrics.name: seder
rubrics_metrics.description: The ritualized dinner held in Jewish homes on the first night or first two nights of Passover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain meaning of 'seder' ('order'), its commemoration of escape from Egypt, features (special foods, reading of the Haggadah) and rituals.

rubrics_metrics.name: seizure
rubrics_metrics.description: See epilepsy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference to epilepsy entry for definition and usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: senior housing, senior apartments
rubrics_metrics.description: Age-restricted multi-unit housing with self-contained living units for older adults, usually aged 55+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that senior apartments generally do not offer additional services such as meals or transportation.

rubrics_metrics.name: senior, senior citizen
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms for older people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sparingly; can be discriminatory. Preferred terminology is 'older adults'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sephardi
rubrics_metrics.description: A Jew of Portuguese, Spanish or North African descent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pronounced 'suh-FAR-dee.' Originally meant Jews descended from Iberian Peninsula; now often means Jews who are not Ashkenazim. Plural Sephardim. See Ashkenazi.

rubrics_metrics.name: seroconversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientifically observable alteration of blood or other fluids from HIV-negative to HIV-positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verb is 'seroconvert.' See HIV entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: seronegative
rubrics_metrics.description: Synonymous with HIV-negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See HIV.

rubrics_metrics.name: seropositive
rubrics_metrics.description: Synonymous with HIV-positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See HIV.

rubrics_metrics.name: service animal/assistance animal/guide dog/Seeing Eye dog
rubrics_metrics.description: Service animals are trained animals, mostly dogs, which provide services to people with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use federal ADA definition: any guide dog, signal dog or other animal trained to do work or perform tasks for benefit of an individual with a disability. Service animal, assistance animal and guide dog acceptable. Avoid 'Seeing Eye dog' as Seeing Eye is a registered trademark. Note contentious issues about licensure/certification; when in doubt refer to federal definition and DOJ FAQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: sex change
rubrics_metrics.description: An antiquated term for gender transition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid; see gender transition or sex reassignment guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: sexual orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes an individual's enduring physical, romantic and/or emotional attraction to another person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gender identity and sexual orientation are not the same. Transgender people may be straight, lesbian, gay, or bisexual. Provide example regarding a person who transitions and their orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: sexual preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Politically charged term implying sexuality is a conscious choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid; use 'sexual orientation' instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: sexual reassignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The medical and surgical process by which transgender people change physical sexual characteristics to reflect their gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include surgery and/or hormone therapy. Avoid overemphasizing surgery in transition coverage; note not all transgender people choose or can afford surgery. Avoid outdated term 'sex change'.

rubrics_metrics.name: sexually transmitted infection (STI)
rubrics_metrics.description: STIs were formerly known as STDs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'sexually transmitted infection' to emphasize infection can occur without symptoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shabbat
rubrics_metrics.description: Hebrew word for Sabbath; Jewish Sabbath from sundown Friday to sundown Saturday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe practices (lighting candles Friday night, special family meal, Torah reading, Shabbat lunch), end with havdalah ritual, and note Orthodox restrictions on certain activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: shaman
rubrics_metrics.description: A spiritual leader in a tribal society who heals people by channeling spirits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term is a description not a formal title; do not capitalize, even when used with a name. Sometimes called medicine man or witch doctor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shariah
rubrics_metrics.description: The way or path that Muslims follow to achieve God’s will on Earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe principles come from Quran, hadith and other considerations depending on sect; emphasizes righteous living, community protection and establishing a just society.

rubrics_metrics.name: sheesha
rubrics_metrics.description: See argilah, argeelah.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: sheikh
rubrics_metrics.description: Title used by many Islamic clergymen and as a secular title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize when used before a name, lowercase otherwise. Note alternate uses: leader of family, village, or tribe in Arab communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shiism, Shiite
rubrics_metrics.description: Shiism is the smaller of the two major branches of Islam; followers called Shiites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Shiite' instead of Shi’ah unless in a quote or part of a name. Uppercase in all uses. See Islam, Sunni.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shinto
rubrics_metrics.description: Japan’s indigenous religion with no formal doctrine, stressing nature, harmony and personal cleanliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note historical state status and post-WWII separation from the state; capitalize in references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shiva
rubrics_metrics.description: A popular representation of God in Hinduism; worshipped as lord of time and change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pronounced 'SHEE-vah.' Note Brahma and Vishnu distinctions and alternate spelling Siva ('SEE-vah').

rubrics_metrics.name: short stature
rubrics_metrics.description: See dwarf/little person/midget/short stature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference; use preferred, non-offensive terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: sickle-cell anemia
rubrics_metrics.description: Inherited chronic anemia found chiefly among blacks, characterized by abnormal red blood cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe pathophysiology and treatment options; acceptable to describe a person as 'someone with sickle-cell anemia'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sikhism
rubrics_metrics.description: Religion originating in 15th-century Punjab; followers called Sikhs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide pronunciation, core beliefs (equality, rejection of caste), history (Guru Nanak, 10 gurus, formation of Khalsa in 1699), Five Kakaars and Guru Granth Sahib as lasting teacher, no formal clergy though spiritual guides may be called gurus (capitalize before a name). Capitalize titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Singh
rubrics_metrics.description: A last name shared by all men who practice the Sikh religion, meaning 'lion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originated with Guru Gobind Singh to signify equality; note naming customs.

rubrics_metrics.name: sister, sista
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms referring to family member or affectionate/respectful name for a church member, sorority member or another black woman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of appropriateness in news copy; may use in quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: skullcap
rubrics_metrics.description: A small, close-fitting headpiece worn in some religious traditions, particularly by men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate names include yarmulke or kippa (Jews), zucchetto (Roman Catholic prelates) and kufi (Muslims).

rubrics_metrics.name: slant
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid use to describe eyes; it is a racial slur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See eye shape.

rubrics_metrics.name: slavery
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical overview of slavery in the American colonies and U.S.; describes brutality, Middle Passage, resistance and abolition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize with Underground Railroad, Harriet Tubman, Civil War, Emancipation Proclamation and 13th Amendment; see related entries such as Juneteenth and Middle Passage.

rubrics_metrics.name: slope
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid use to describe eyes; a racial slur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See eye shape.

rubrics_metrics.name: sodomy laws
rubrics_metrics.description: State laws historically used to selectively persecute gay people; ruled unconstitutional in Lawrence v. Texas (2003).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using 'sodomy' to describe gay, lesbian or bisexual relationships or sexuality. See sodomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: soul food
rubrics_metrics.description: Cuisine originally popular in the South and traditionally eaten by black people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note origins in slavery, typical dishes (collard greens, fried chicken, ham hocks, black-eyed peas, yams, cornbread) and cultural context.

rubrics_metrics.name: South Asia
rubrics_metrics.description: Term to represent the southern region of the Asian continent, including specific countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define geographic bounds; mention alternate term 'Indian subcontinent' and list included countries (Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal, India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka).

rubrics_metrics.name: South Asian
rubrics_metrics.description: Collective term for people from Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note 'Desi American' is used by some but not all; check with source/individual to confirm preferred identification and ensure that identifying race/ethnicity is essential to the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: South Asian diaspora
rubrics_metrics.description: People of South Asian heritage living outside South Asia due to colonial legacy and immigration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention countries with substantial South Asian populations (Fiji, Guyana, Mauritius, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago, Malaysia, Singapore, South Africa, UAE, UK, US).

rubrics_metrics.name: South Asian names
rubrics_metrics.description: Naming conventions in South Asia and the diaspora vary by community, religion and generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask interview subjects which name is first name vs surname. Don't generalize; note presence of one-word names and variation across Hindus, Sikhs, Muslims, Christians, Jews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Southeast Asia, Southeastern Asia
rubrics_metrics.description: Subregion of Asia south of China, east of India, west of New Guinea and north of Australia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define two geographic regions: Maritime Southeast Asia (Brunei, Christmas Island, East Malaysia, East Timor, Indonesia, Philippines, Singapore) and Mainland Southeast Asia/Indochina (Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar/Burma, Thailand, Vietnam, West Malaysia). Note seismic/volcanic activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Southern Cross
rubrics_metrics.description: Confederate battle flag used during the Civil War, offensive to some black Americans because it represents Confederacy and slavery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe appearance and note its appropriation by KKK and extremist groups and contemporary controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spanglish
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal hybrid of Spanish and English used by bilingual speakers who switch languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe code-switching and pragmatic reasons (one language describes better than the other).

rubrics_metrics.name: spastic/spaz
rubrics_metrics.description: See cerebral palsy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference; avoid offensive slang derived from medical terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: special rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Politically charged term used by opponents of civil rights for the LGBT community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid; use 'LGBT rights', 'equal rights' or 'gay and lesbian rights' as alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: special/special needs/functional needs
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Special needs' historically used to refer to people with disabilities or programs serving them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'special' as stigmatizing; prefer to cite specific disability or use 'functional needs' when a term is required. Exception: government references or formal organization names.

rubrics_metrics.name: spina bifida
rubrics_metrics.description: Neural tube defect where spinal column does not fully close in the womb; most common neural tube defect in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe four types and range of complications; acceptable phrasing: 'someone with spina bifida' followed by brief explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: sponsorship
rubrics_metrics.description: A movement connecting people in authority with high-potential employees to advocate for their advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention formal programs to improve diversity, equity and inclusion in management and leadership; added April 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: sports stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid characterizations of black athletes as naturally superior to other athletes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such depictions echo slavery-era 'bucks' stereotypes; avoid reductive racialized descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sri
rubrics_metrics.description: A term of respect among some Indians, similar to 'mister.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: The word originates from Greek for 'fixed impression' and was popularized by Walter Lippmann.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples and caution against relying on stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stonewall
rubrics_metrics.description: The Stonewall Inn site in NYC of protests after a police raid in 1969 regarded as birth of modern gay civil rights movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize historical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: straight
rubrics_metrics.description: Term meaning heterosexual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a noun, use 'heterosexual' or 'straight person'.

rubrics_metrics.name: stricken with
rubrics_metrics.description: See victim of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to preferred phrasing in 'victim of' entry; avoid 'stricken with'.

rubrics_metrics.name: stuttering/stammering
rubrics_metrics.description: A speech disorder characterized by repeated or prolonged words, sounds or syllables affecting fluency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'stuttering' over 'stammering.' Do not call someone 'a stutterer'; use people-first language ('a person who stutters'). Refer to sources (NIDCD, Mayo Clinic, National Stuttering Association) and to new DSM term 'childhood-onset fluency disorder' (not yet widely used). Refer to treatment possibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: suffers from
rubrics_metrics.description: See victim of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference; prefer neutral phrasing over 'suffers from' when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: suicide
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on reporting suicide to reduce risk of contagion and avoid stigma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'commits suicide'; use 'died by suicide' or 'took his own life.' Reporting cautions: Placement—do not dramatize or put on front page or use 'suicide' in headline; Details—avoid exact locations and methods; Photos/videos—avoid images of location/method or dramatic grieving/memorials; Language—avoid 'committed/ succeeded/failed'; Don’t oversimplify causes—suicide is complex, often involves mental health/substance issues and multiple factors. Link to Reporting on Suicide and CDC and Dart Center resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: suicide bombing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of explosives carried to a target on the body of the attacker or in a vehicle operated by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially fearsome because attacker cannot be bargained with; note possible origins (early 1980s Tamil Tigers) and similarity to kamikaze.

rubrics_metrics.name: suicide contagion
rubrics_metrics.description: Research shows certain types of news coverage can increase likelihood of suicide in vulnerable individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk increases with explicit description of method, dramatic/graphic headlines or images, and repeated sensationalized coverage. Provide references and see 'suicide' entry for responsible coverage guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunni
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced 'SOO-nee.' The largest denomination in Islam (about 85% of Muslims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plural 'Sunnis'; see Shiism, Shiite.

rubrics_metrics.name: swastika
rubrics_metrics.description: An ancient symbol popular among Hindus, Jains and Buddhists meaning auspiciousness; Nazi use perverted the symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain religious significance and the distinction from the Nazi swastika.

rubrics_metrics.name: systemic racism
rubrics_metrics.description: Social values that support personal and institutional discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how people of color must adapt to a society not built for them while white people fit in; see institutional racism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tagalog
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced tah-GAH-log. The official language of the Philippines among many regional dialects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taipeng Revolution
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the bloodiest conflicts in world history (likely intended Taiping Rebellion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide historical context about massive casualties and central government fears of separatist movements; mention contemporaneous timing with American Civil War.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tao
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced 'Dow.' The ever-changing energy of the universe in Taoism; unknowable and cannot be defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast with Confucianism where Tao is conduct governed by universal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taoism, Daoism
rubrics_metrics.description: A school of philosophical and religious teachings stemming from Tao.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pronounced 'DOW-ism.' Note historical suppression in Maoist China and post-1980s revival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tejano
rubrics_metrics.description: A Texan of Mexican descent; derives from 'Coahuiltejano.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe cultural elements (folk music, Tex-Mex cuisine) and historical bilingualism shaping Tejano language.

rubrics_metrics.name: telenovela
rubrics_metrics.description: A type of 'limited-run' television drama popular in Latin America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different from U.S. soap operas: fixed duration, episodes five to six days a week, average ~120 episodes per telenovela.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thai names
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically personal name first, family name second, often long multi-syllable names, especially if Chinese.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of name order and complexity; verify name order with sources when necessary.
